claims.text: Headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards redefined 'fully closed' to mean 'pay us first'
claims.note: IRGC said the strait was closed until the US lifts its blockade (Al Jazeera). No IRGC statement about payment for passage found for 18-19 April.

claims.text: Subheadline: dictatorships charging tolls instead of shooting missiles
claims.note: Rhetorical; also contradicted by reports of IRGC boats firing on ships on 18 April.

claims.text: Strait of Hormuz 'fully closed' until the US lifts its blockade on Iranian ports, according to the Revolutionary Guards
claims.note: Al Jazeera, 18 April: Iran closes Hormuz again over US blockade; closure came less than 24 hours after Iran declared it open.

claims.text: Iranian closures come with price lists attached; Tehran says it is just managing traffic flow
claims.note: No 18-19 April source for a price list or 'managing traffic flow'.

claims.text: Tehran fired warning shots at commercial vessels earlier this week
claims.note: UKMTO: two IRGC gunboats fired on a tanker on 18 April (same day as the closure, not earlier in the week), with no VHF challenge; tanker and crew safe. Reuters said at least two ships reported being fired on.

claims.text: Trump called it 'blackmail', saying America won't be extorted over Hormuz
claims.note: Trump said on 18 April Iran cannot 'blackmail us' over the Strait of Hormuz. 'In a video statement' not confirmed (he spoke to reporters per most reports); dropped.

claims.text: Aides kept Trump out of the Iran war room this week, fearing his 'impatience wouldn't help', according to the Wall Street Journal
claims.note: WSJ reported aides kept him out of the Situation Room during the rescue of airmen from a jet downed over Iran in early April, not 'this week'; 'they believed his impatience wouldn't be helpful'. White House called the report 'fake news' (https://www.timesofisrael.com/trump-managing-iran-war-based-on-conflicting-caprices-that-blindside-his-aides-report/).

claims.text: Lebanon reopened key routes in the south as repairs continue
claims.note: LBCI: Lebanese army reopened key south roads and began bridge repairs after Israeli strikes.

claims.note: Launch on 19 April from the Sinpo area toward the sea, per South Korea's military. AFP text not found (Arab News copy carries an AFP photo only); reattributed to CTV News.

edits.headline: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz again over US blockade
edits.subheadline: The Revolutionary Guards said the strait would stay closed until the US lifted its blockade of Iranian ports, Al Jazeera reported.
editorialBody: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until the US lifted its blockade of Iranian ports, Al Jazeera reported. The announcement came less than a day after Iran declared the strait open.
Two Revolutionary Guards gunboats fired on a tanker on 18 April, the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said, according to Lokmat Times. The tanker and its crew were safe.
President Trump said Iran could not "blackmail" the US over the Strait of Hormuz, Khaleej Times reported.

Trump's aides kept him out of the Situation Room during the rescue of airmen from a US jet downed over Iran because they believed his impatience would not help, the Wall Street Journal reported. The White House called the report "fake news", according to the Times of Israel.
The Lebanese army reopened key roads in south Lebanon and began repairing bridges damaged by Israeli strikes, LBCI reported.
North Korea fired several short-range ballistic missiles towards the sea on 19 April, South Korea's military said, according to CTV News.
In Japan, an adult bear found in a residential area of Sendai was shot under the country's emergency culling system, Jiji Press reported.
In India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi promised women in West Bengal Rs 36,000 a year if his party won the state election, Outlook India reported.
Darshan Kumar, brother of T-Series founder Gulshan Kumar, died in Delhi at the age of 70, IANS reported. The singer Mika Singh paid tribute to him, according to LatestLY.
